You know I thought we were very fortunate to  come in at the break, uh, nil-nil. You know,  
we—we didn't get started at all right from the  first minute. St Mirren put us under pressure,  
and I thought they were better in—in  most areas on the park in terms of, uh,  
energy levels, picking up second balls,  you know, putting crosses into the box.
The one thing we can be thankful of is how  well the guys at the back defended the box  
in those difficult moments, and Jack Walton  as well when called upon—having to make saves  
and come for crosses. Uh, we had  some harsh words at halftime. We  
weren't happy with what we’d seen, um,  and the players are honest enough to  
admit that. And I thought we saw a better  version of ourselves in the second 45.
And you know, if you were to look at the  stats from the first half to the second half,  
we had far more shots, far more  shots on target, lots more, uh,  
crosses into the box, and got into more  dangerous areas in that second half. Um,  
you know, two or three goalmouth scrambles,  you know, a really tight offside goal.
Um, yeah, I thought it was a really entertaining  game of football. I would imagine from a neutral’s  
perspective, it had end-to-end stuff. Uh,  I’m sure Steven Robinson will be extremely  
disappointed not to have taken something  given the one-on-one chance at nil-nil and  
then obviously the penalty opportunity to  make the, uh, to make it a—a level game.
But, you know, credit to Jack Walton  in those two instances—the one-on-one,  
it’s a brilliant save, and the  penalty, uh, the same. You know,  
chooses to go the right way, and,  um, Kevin van Veen, I have to say,  
does really well to react as well and follow  the ball in. So, a magnificent three points.
Our away form is, uh, has been exceptional  all season. I think we’re the second in the  
league table in terms of, uh, points  return on the road behind Celtic. And,  
uh, that’s credit to the group for the test of  character. It’s not easy going away from home,  
hostile environments, um, you  know, but the boys managed to  
find a way to win the game today,  and that’s the most pleasing aspect.
Goalkeepers were in pretty tremendous form,  
but it’s going to take something special to  win it. And you know, the goal clearly was—
Yeah, definitely. I mean, you know, the  corner was something that we’d worked on,  
um, yesterday in training, and, uh, it was almost  perfect. I just think there was a slight touch on  
it in the middle of the penalty area, which then  deemed Vassell to be offside. But it was something  
that we tried to target in the build-up to  the game, and it almost worked perfectly.
Um, but yeah, I mean, you know, the St Mirren  goalkeeper made two or three big saves, um,  
but as—as Jack Walton showed over the whole piece,  you know, a draw was probably a fair result. But  
I’m delighted to be sitting here having, uh, kept  a clean sheet and picked up all three points.
You send on attacking moments you’re looking for.
Yeah, I mean, numerous occasions this year  where, um, substitutions have come on and  
made real positive impacts for us. And we tried  to be brave with the—the substitutions. You know,  
we finished the game with three strikers  on the pitch with van Veen alongside Moult  
and Delboy. We wanted to have a go. We weren’t  satisfied with the draw, and, um, it paid off.
You know, sometimes as a manager, uh, you  know, the decisions I made in the Hearts  
game when we were drawing nil-nil—you  know, those substitutions that I made,  
uh, and the shape of the team that  I changed to didn’t work. Today,  
thankfully, the substitutions paid off,  and that’s—that’s the game that we’re in.
So, um, it’s a huge victory for us.  Um, it’s the start of the last block  
of 11 games prior to the split, and, um, we’ve  put ourselves in a really good position now.
How close was Louis to not making  it today? ‘Cause I know there were  
a few guys touch and go. Was—was he one of them?
He was, yeah. I mean, we kind  of wrapped him up in cotton wool  
yesterday. He joined in with the group,  but he was very much non-contact. Um,  
the players were told not to go near him. He  had an injection, um, in his shoulder about  
two hours before kickoff to try and numb the  pain, and, um—and he made himself available.
And that’s the type of character that he is.  They’re the types of people that we want at the  
club. And, um, you know, he comes on in those  big moments and, you know, he’s a real natural  
goal scorer. And I don’t think he’ll have scored  many better than that over the last few years.
I was going to say, I don’t think  as many strikers in Scotland are  
capable of that goal technically, just,  you know, your moment of inspiration.
Yeah, absolutely. You know, it’s the—the good  strikers, their brain tends to work a little  
bit quicker than the rest of ours. And, um,  you know, he just recognized that situation,  
managed to pop the ball up into the air,  and, um, you know, a brilliant technique.
I would imagine the shoulder he  landed on would be pretty sore,  
uh, once that injection wears off,  but it’s all worth it. You know,  
in front of our own supporters as well—a  great traveling support. He gets booked  
for the celebrations, but the emotions got  the better of him for jumping into the crowd.
But, uh, a great moment, a great feeling  for the group. And, um, you know, not only  
does it open up that gap between ourselves  and St Mirren now to 10 points, uh, it also  
pushes us that little bit closer to Rangers  as well, who we’ve got a big game tomorrow.
title: JIM GOODWIN FULL POST MATCH PRESS CONFERENCE | ST MIRREN 0-1 DUNDEE UNITED
